headline: Germany took Austria in March and the Sudetenland by agreement in September, then burned the synagogues in November
texture: German troops occupied Austria on March 12 and the annexation was declared the next day. In September, Britain, France, Italy and Germany agreed at Munich that Germany could have the Sudetenland, and Poland and Hungary put in claims of their own. Hitler broke the agreement on October 21. On the night of November 9 the synagogues burned across Germany, along with Jewish shops and homes.

Orson Welles broadcast The War of the Worlds on October 30 as a series of news bulletins, and enough listeners took it literally to make the papers for a week. Superman appeared in Action Comics on April 18. The minimum wage became law in the United States on October 24, at twenty-five cents an hour.

Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs went wide in February and took $3,996,000 in rentals, more than any film had. You Can't Take It with You was fifth and won Best Picture. The Yankees swept the Cubs in the World Series, their third title in a row, and Boys Town came second at the box office with Spencer Tracy playing a priest.

world.munich_agreement.label: Munich Agreement
world.munich_agreement.value: German, Italian, British and French leaders agreed to Germany's demands on the Sudetenland
world.munich_agreement.detail: Poland and Hungary pressed claims on Czechoslovak territory as soon as the Czech government capitulated. Hitler broke the agreement on October 21, and Hungary was awarded the Felvidek region on November 2.

world.kristallnacht.label: Kristallnacht
world.kristallnacht.value: The night of broken glass, when synagogues, shops and homes were attacked across Germany

world.poland_lithuania.value: Poland demanded normal diplomatic relations under threat

world.vatican_franco.label: Vatican recognises Franco
world.vatican_franco.value: Recognised his government while the Spanish Civil War was still being fought

radio.war_of_the_worlds.label: The War of the Worlds broadcast
radio.war_of_the_worlds.value: Orson Welles presented the invasion as a sequence of news bulletins

film.gross.label: Highest-grossing films, US domestic rentals
value: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, $3,996,000, RKO and Walt Disney
You Can't Take It with You, $2,182,000, Columbia
film.gross.detail: Rentals, the distributor share rather than the ticket window total, so roughly half what a gross figure would say. Snow White had opened in December of the previous year and went wide in February.

film.best_picture.label: Best Picture
film.best_picture.value: You Can't Take It with You

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a theatre. The biggest film of the year was a cartoon, which nobody had expected to work at feature length.

culture.superman.label: Superman appears
culture.superman.value: First published in Action Comics number one

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: A year of governments agreeing to things they knew would not hold, and a radio play about an invasion that some listeners believed because the format was the same one carrying the news from Europe.

prices.min_wage.label: Federal minimum wage
prices.min_wage.detail: The basic rate for covered nonfarm workers, as in effect on December 31. It became law in October.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: New York Yankees swept the Chicago Cubs, four games to none

notes: Research pass July 2026. First year with a prices section: the federal minimum wage series starts here, at the rate in effect on December 31. The claim that the Welles broadcast made the papers for a week, and that Snow White outsold any previous film, are general knowledge rather than statements from the year pages. Spencer Tracy playing a priest in Boys Town is likewise general knowledge of the film.
